subject: Ironcrest: private cluster throughput collapse / 502 storm — exec attention
messages:
From: Ironcrest Ops <ops@ironcrest.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] On-prem cluster: sudden throughput collapse and repeating 502s

Jonas --

We just hit a hard failure on our Ironcrest private deployment (vpc-onprem) after a routine kernel patch and a model-serving config bounce at ~08:20. Symptoms: sustained throughput drop (~60%), p95 latency up from 180ms to 2.4s, and a storm of 502s across the primary shard. This is affecting production search indexing and our internal webhooks.

We collected the following and attached a compressed trace: svc_trace_20270912.log.gz. The trace shows repeated worker restarts and long stalls in the model server process.

Can someone triage ASAP? We are on-call and can provide access to the cluster console and metrics.

- Samir Rao (on-call)
Ops Lead, Ironcrest
ops@ironcrest.ai

Attachments: svc_trace_20270912.log.gz
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ironcrest Ops <ops@ironcrest.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 08:52:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] On-prem cluster: sudden throughput collapse and repeating 502s

Samir / Samir's team —

Thanks for the quick flag. I'm looping in Marissa and Connor for immediate triage and Evelyn from CS to coordinate the customer comms and any contractual asks.

Quick asks to help us prioritize:
- Can you confirm whether the kernel patch included any libc/epoll or network driver changes?
- Can you provide the full system metrics for the shard: CPU, mem, disk I/O, and network from 07:30->09:00?
- Is the 502 pattern localized to a single hot shard or across multiple hosts?

Connor / Marissa — initial ask is to check for process-level deadlocks (blocked threads, stuck epoll) and KV cache stalls. If we confirm a deadlock pattern, mitigation options: reduce concurrency on the model server, temporarily switch the shard to a fallback model (lower memory profile), or scale an additional worker pool if capacity allows.

I will prepare an exec summary and involve Laura if this looks like a contractual SLA exposure.

Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ironcrest Ops <ops@ironcrest.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:18:44 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] On-prem cluster: sudden throughput collapse and repeating 502s

Jonas / Samir —

Quick triage update (running on-call checks now):
- Local reproduction: we replayed a subset of the trace on a staging node. Observed long thread stalls inside the serving worker around the attention/kcache path. Several threads show 'futex' waits; looks like contention on a shared mmap'd KV cache region.
- Symptoms line up with a concurrency deadlock where the background cache eviction thread is contending with decode workers — under patch conditions this can amplify and cause worker restarts -> 502s.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered by risk):
1) Turn down max_concurrency on the affected model process to 4 (from 12) to break contention.
2) Enable the fast-evict flag for KV cache (non-disruptive toggle) to reduce long-lived locks.
3) If (1)-(2) fail, switch the shard to 'gpt-medium-quant' fallback while we push a deadlock fix.

Connor is pulling kernel logs and will share a kvcache_dump_0927.json. We're preparing a reload that applies (1) and (2) which should be low risk. Expect rollout in ~30 mins if you approve.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kvcache_dump_0927.json
From: Elena Park <elena.park@ironcrest.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@ironcrest.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] On-prem cluster: sudden throughput collapse and repeating 502s

Jonas / Marissa —

This has escalated to our CTO. We need an exec-level note: what happened, short-term mitigations, and an ETA for root cause and permanent fix. We also need to know whether this breach materially impacts our SLA (we are in a renewal window and the legal team is watching).

In the meantime, we need confirmation on:
- Whether the mitigation plan will cause any data loss or change in inference outputs (we rely on stable outputs for downstream scoring).
- Whether Redwood can commit to temporary credits if this maps to a SLA violation.

Please provide an exec summary and proposed agenda for a 30-min sync between our CTO and Redwood execs.

Thanks,
Elena Park
VP Engineering, Ironcrest
elena.park@ironcrest.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@ironcrest.ai>, Ironcrest Ops <ops@ironcrest.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] On-prem cluster: sudden throughput collapse and repeating 502s

Elena / Ironcrest leadership —

Exec summary (for CTO sync):
- What happened: after a kernel/driver patch and a config bounce, the on-prem serving runtime entered a high-contention state where the KV cache eviction path contends with decode worker threads. That contention can escalate into a deadlock under certain concurrency profiles, causing worker restarts and 502s.
- Short-term mitigations (we are executing now):
  1) Reduce model max_concurrency to 4 on the affected shard (done at 12:05 PST). Expected impact: immediate reduction in 502s and lower p95; throughput will be reduced temporarily but service becomes stable.
  2) Toggle fast-evict for KV cache (done at 12:08 PST). Expected impact: reduces long-lived locks, low risk to inference outputs.
  3) Prepped fallback switch to 'gpt-medium-quant' if instability persists (not applied).
- Risk to inference quality: mitigations (1) and (2) do not change model weights or tokenization; they may slightly increase per-request latency under heavy load but not change outputs. Fallback model would change outputs and is only used as last resort.
- ETA for permanent fix: Connor and the runtime team will ship a patch to address lock ordering and introduce a lightweight eviction path within 48-72 hours; full verification and backout plan within 5 business days.
- Customer ask & Redwood offer: we acknowledge the impact. We will open a formal SLA review. Pending legal review, we can propose a temporary credit against the impacted invoice while root cause is resolved; I'll coordinate finance and legal.

Action items & links:
- Jira: IRN-4123 created for the fix and postmortem (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/IRN-4123)
- Artifacts attached: svc_trace_20270912.log.gz, kvcache_dump_0927.json
- Next steps: 30-min exec sync requested. Proposed times: Today 14:00, 15:00 PST. Please confirm.

I'll bring Laura Bennett (VP, Customer Success) to the sync to discuss credit/contracting if needed.

Thanks for the cooperation — we'll keep this thread updated with progress notes.

Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
